chapter: Favorite bands, advice and family reflections
title: Teeth, his dentist and Red Allen's gold
summary: He wants his teeth fixed and praises Dr. Samson; Red Allen had much gold and lived in the Bronx.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: You said one of the things you want to do is get some new glasses and get your teeth fixed.
Yeah. I don't have no trouble playing without teeth now. I have a small bridge here but I don't want it like that. I want it right.
Do you have a dentist that you're planning to go to?
Dr. Samson. And I want down, the first time I went to Dr. Samson was in 1929, you weren't even born then. I got a filling that he cleaned. It was half a
tooth to show you how good he is. Does it look like half a tooth?
It does look like half a tooth?
That's it. It looks like a whole tooth. But, it's a half. That's how good he is.
Did Louis Armstrong ever talk to you about his dentist? All the times that he would go to the dentist?
I know it. Red Allen had nothing but a whole lot of gold. He should be rich off of that. ... I don't give a damn. He's dead now. I can't hurt him much talking to him. ...
You used to go visit Red Allen up in the Bronx a lot, huh?
Yeah. A block from my sister. But, I didn't visit that often because he lived on the fifth floor.
